pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart fills the card top to bottom (height 0.869, just over the real range). The awning nearly reaches the top edge and the wheels sit on the tiles near the bottom, so it reads as packed in, like the tight real cards. B: the helmet sits fully contained and dead centre on a wide steel floor, with even air around it. Its 0.133 margin is above the real maximum of 0.098, and the riveted floor takes up the lower quarter without adding to the read.
pairs.fix: Draw the helmet larger and closer, turned a little to one side, so it nearly touches the left and right edges. Show only a thin strip of plain floor under it, with no plates or rivets.

pairs.difference: A: one topiary stands slightly left of centre and is the only focus. The hedge and path stay low in contrast behind it. B: the planet reads first, but two moons in the top right and lower left, the sparkles and the pink cloud bands all pull the eye away. The ring tip almost touches the right edge (margin 0.028). The extra props match the lessons, where the generated lighthouse gained a lifebuoy and bushes.
pairs.fix: Remove the two small moons and the pink clouds. Keep one large planet on a plain deep-blue background with a few faint stars, and leave clear space between the ring tips and the card edges.

pairs.difference: A: the orange case sits upper left and the earbuds and cord trail to the lower right, giving an off-centre diagonal, though the thin cord is weak at thumbnail size. B: the UFO is a flat wide band dead centre on the concentric rings, 0.475 tall against a real minimum of 0.581. Large empty pink areas sit above and below it, so the card looks centred by formula and under-filled vertically.
pairs.fix: Bring the UFO closer and tilt it more steeply so the dome and underside both show, making it fill about two thirds of the card height. Set it slightly off the ring centre.

pairs.difference: A: the submarine fills the width (0.863) with the periscope rising to upper right, centred and clear against the dark green glow. B: the rocket is tilted and fills the height (0.825), clear against the cyan rays. All measures for both are inside the real ranges, and both read instantly with nothing competing, so composition gives no reason to choose.

A: the telescope is a thin diagonal with a spindly tripod, covering only 0.163 of the card against a real minimum of 0.233. Empty purple sits at upper left and bare deck at the bottom, so the hero looks light for its frame. B: the ship's wheel is frontal and symmetric, a little contained (margin 0.105), but it is a solid mass and reads at once. Both share a curved deck horizon, so this is a weak call based on hero mass.
pairs.fix: Draw the telescope much bigger and thicker, with the large end pushing toward the top right corner and the tripod cropped short, so it fills the card rather than crossing it as a thin line.

pairs.difference: A: the robot stands upright, frontal and centred, fully contained with air around its thin arms and antennae. The wall and floor split the card, and the card looks staged like the contained generated lesson heroes. B: the vending machine is a solid three-quarter block filling more of the card (0.422) and sits a touch right of centre, which is closer to the angled real heroes. All numbers are in range, so this rests only on the pose and containment.
pairs.fix: Turn the robot three-quarters and bring it closer, with a thicker body filling more of the card and its feet close to the bottom edge.

pairs.difference: A: the lion on its plinth fills the card (box 0.935 wide) and reads first, though the trees and curving path behind it are busy. B: the envelope and photos are tilted and fill the card on a plain green swirl. The hero is clean, but the small village scene inside the photo is detailed at thumbnail size. Both are large and instantly named, and each resembles real cards (the motel scene and the towel tilt), so composition does not separate them.

A: the spyglass is small on a tonal cyan stripe (area 0.168, height 0.452, both below the real range). It leaves a lot of empty card, but background and hero are clearly ordered. B: the ray gun is well sized and angled, but the hard yellow and cyan stripes are as loud as the hero and cut behind it. The green muzzle ball also sits close to the left edge. Real backgrounds stay in one hue family, as in the rays and checks on the real cards. This is a low-confidence call because A's size numbers argue the other way.
pairs.fix: Replace the yellow stripes with soft stripes of two close blue tones so the red gun is the only strong colour, and keep clear space around the green muzzle ball.

pairs.difference: A: the control panel is centred low and wide, but the glowing blue floor strips in the bottom third and the orange wall stripes pull attention away from it. At thumbnail size the panel breaks into coloured dots with no single focus, so it is slower to name. B: the fruit plate fills the card on a diagonal, the watermelon wedge is an immediate large focus, and the plain wood stays quiet.
pairs.fix: Remove the glowing floor lights and the panel lines in the floor. Make the round radar screen much larger as the single focus, reduce the rows of buttons, and bring the console closer on a plain background.

pairs.difference: A: the flower bed is centred and fully contained on a plain pink set, with clear space around it. B: the Ferris wheel is cropped by the top, right and bottom edges (margin 0, height 0.898, above the range). This is a bold crop like the real lighthouse and plane, and the generated lesson cards never did it. B's numbers are out of range while its behaviour looks real, and A's numbers are in range, so the evidence conflicts.

A: the gate and pillars span the card as a frontal scene. The measured area looks low (0.157), probably because the mask caught only the gate, not the pillars. B: the station reads instantly, but its solar panels run almost to both side edges (width 0.986, margin 0.005), making a near-touch tangent rather than a clean crop or clear gap. The bright Earth arc with white clouds across the bottom and the magenta sky compete with the hero.
pairs.fix: Shrink the solar panels or crop them firmly off the card edges. Replace the bright Earth with a darker, simple curve at the very bottom, or remove it, and use a calm single-colour sky.

pairs.difference: A: the boat lies on a strong diagonal, with the pier cropped by the top and left edges and the lily pads kept quiet. It is an off-centre crop like the real plane and lifeguard chair. B: the pod is dead centre, frontal and symmetric, contained like the generated lessons (margin 0.037). The glowing rings on the floor, the lit arcs and the bright columns repeat the hero's light and compete with its glass door.
pairs.fix: Turn the pod three-quarters and crop it slightly at one side. Remove the glowing floor rings and ceiling arcs, and set it against a plain soft blue backdrop.

pattern: Generated cards tend to keep the hero fully contained, centred and upright or frontal, with even space on all sides. Real cards are more willing to crop, push off-centre or run a strong diagonal. Generated cards also add scene props and glowing set dressing, such as moons, floor lights, light rings and Earth arcs, which compete with the hero. They also leave near-touch tangents at the card edge instead of a clear gap or a firm crop, and they use loud backgrounds where real ones stay quiet and in one hue family. Size alone is a weak signal: most measures overlap the real ranges, and several out-of-range values fall on cards that otherwise look real (p08 A, p10 B, p11 A).
